headlines.title: Preliminary 4.1 magnitude and 4.5 magnitude quakes strike in Northern California
headlines.description: A preliminary 4.1 magnitude earthquake followed by a preliminary 4.5 magnitude struck in Northern California, according to the United States Geological Survey. The first quake, with preliminary magnitude of 4.1, hit at 3:20 p.m. and was centered 19.26 miles northwest of Covelo and approximately 210 miles north of San Francisco, the USGS said. According to the USGS, a second earthquake, with a preliminary magnitude of 4.5, hit a minute later and was centered in the same area. The temblors come after the Covelo area was rattled by a 4.0 magnitude earthquake on Tuesday. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. headlines.title: Deadly mass shooting near Morgan Hill: FBI joins investigation, offers $20K reward
headlines.description: The FBI has joined the investigation into last month’s deadly mass shooting at a pop-up birthday party near Morgan Hill and is offering a reward of up to $20,000 for information leading to an arrest, the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office said Wednesday. Seven people were shot, one fatally, during the party on Saturday, July 25, at a rural property along Hale Avenue, officials said. The party, which was advertised on social media, drew hundreds of attendees. The sheriff’s office said the FBI’s involvement in the investigation will bring “significant federal resources and technical support” into play as authorities work to identify the person or persons responsible. “With hundreds of people in attendance, someone knows something,” Santa Clara County Sheriff Robert Jonsen said in a statement. “We’ve asked for the FBI’s assistance, and we are calling on our community to help identify those responsible for this heinous crime. We are grateful the FBI is stepping forward and encouraging others to do the same.” Anyone who was in the area at the time of the shooting and captured photos, videos or other forms of digital content is encouraged to upload their files via the FBI’s digital media tip line. “Those responsible for this senseless shooting should know that the FBI and our law enforcement partners at the Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office will use every available resource to identify and hold them accountable,” FBI San Francisco Special Agent in Charge Scott Schelble said in a statement. “The FBI is offering a reward of up to $20,000 because we believe someone has information that can help move this investigation forward. No piece of information is too small, and your tip could make a difference in bringing justice to the victims, their families, and the Morgan Hill community.” Anyone with additional information about the shooting is asked to call the FBI at 1‑800‑CALL‑FBI. Santa Clara County Jul 27 Santa Clara County Jul 27 Santa Clara County Jul 26 1 killed, several injured in shooting at party near Morgan Hill

headlines.title: South Bay leaders announce strategy to restrict private detention centers
headlines.description: On Wednesday, Bay Area city and county leaders announced a new strategy to try to keep detention centers out of the region. The move comes as ICE seeks to build a facility near Gilroy. After the lawsuit filed by the state and Santa Clara County on a proposed ICE facility near Gilroy has temporarily come to a halt, Bay Area leaders came together on Wednesday to announce a new strategy to keep detention centers out of the region. San Jose is leading the way, with the city council slated to vote on a 45-day temporary moratorium on applications to build detention facilities on private property. “We will first establish a moratorium on any new detention or processing facility developments in our city. When we have this moratorium in place, we will undertake an evaluation of the health, human safety and environmental impacts of these facilities,” San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan said. Bay Area Congressman Sam Liccardo says it’s part of a so-called tool kit he established. He hopes it will give cities and counties a way to look at land use restrictions to keep detention centers out of the region by focusing on conditional use permits. San Jose Jul 29 Santa Clara County Jun 25 Santa Clara County Jun 11 “There are a host of conditions that local communities can apply to a conditional use permit that will substantially impact the ability of ICE to build these facilities and, most importantly, the zoning power, to be able to say they cannot go, for example, in residentially-zoned areas. That’s a powerful tool,” Liccardo said. While federal law supersedes state and local rules, leaders here hope the new approach may offer a legal loophole to keep detention centers out. Community advocates like Ayudando Latinos a Sonar CEO Belinda Arriaga and Jeremy Barouse with the Public Safety Committee (IPEN), who help immigrants, say they support the strategies especially if their applied throughout the region. “We cannot stand one more child to be impacted by the horrors of ICE and detention,” Arriaga said. “This rogue agency conducts warrantless searches, uses excessive force and operates with little legal oversight, when sometimes using children as bait to arrest family members,” Barouse said. NBC Bay Area reached out to the Department of Homeland Security for a comment. In response, DHS issued a statement, saying, “We have no plans for new detention centers in the Silicon Valley region to announce at this time.” Adding that, “ICE has received additional funding for more detention space.” San Jose wants to be the first city to put some of those anti-ICE laws into play. A proposal will go to the Rules and Open Government Committee on Aug. 12; after that, the San Jose City Council will vote on the temporary detention center moratorium on Sept. 15.

headlines.title: 5 arrested in San Francisco child predator sting
headlines.description: The San Francisco Sheriff’s Office and District Attorney’s Office announced the arrests of five men following a three-day undercover operation targeting suspected child predators. The operation, conducted with the help of 10 other law enforcement agencies, took place over three days at the end of July. During the investigation, officers posed as children on several online platforms. Authorities said the men contacted the undercover investigators seeking to meet for lewd acts. According to investigators, four of the men showed up to meet who they believed were children but were instead met by law enforcement officers. The five men arrested are from San Francisco, San Mateo, Daly City and Redwood City. The four men facing felony charges remain in custody. According to sources, one of the men was 50-year-old Ruben Teague, the founder of a boutique investment firm called Cabin Six Advisors. His bio page says he has also served with several prominent other companies and on boards. According to the DA’s Office, Teague was the only one charged with resisting arrest when he tried to run and he remains in custody. The DA’s Office also said the other men, Romauld Santiago, Jorge Nieto and Michael Pauterstill remain in county jail, facing felony charges of meeting a minor for lewd purposes. All of them have been arraigned and pleaded not guilty. Authorities said Jhonny Rodriguez Diaz has also been arraigned, and he’s facing misdemeanor charges since he never actually showed up to the meeting location, so he was released. Sheriff Paul Miyamoto and District Attorney Brooke Jenkins urged parents to use available tools to limit their children’s interactions with strangers online and to have conversations about the dangers of online grooming. “They are very clearly exploitative in nature, very clearly not appropriate relations between an adult and a minor,” Miyamoto said. “You need to be monitoring what those conversations are. You need to be talking to your children about talking to strangers,” Jenkins said. “They think about talking to strangers in person, but we need to talk to them about the dangers of talking to strangers online.” Parents looking for resources on how to protect children online can find information through the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force at icactaskforce.org. Editor’s note: This story was updated to reflect revised arrest numbers provided by authorities. Five people were arrested, not seven.

headlines.title: New policy banning cell phone usage to go into effect at Oakland Unified
headlines.description: The new “bell-to-bell” cell phone policy at Oakland Unified will go into effect Monday for all the schools in the district. Oakland Unified is one of the last big school districts in the state to adapt a district-wide “bell-to-bell” cell phone policy, an important issue on the minds of current and future Montclair Elementary School parents. The new policy, which takes effect Monday morning, prohibits texting, scrolling and calling during the school day. “The bottom line, this is about limiting distractions. We want our kids focused on their job, which is being students, which is learning. It’s about making sure everyone in the classroom is focused on the same thing. It’s about making sure there isn’t online bullying going on,” OUSD Director of Communications John Sasaki said. Elementary school kids will keep phones in classroom locked boxes, and middle and high school students will store them in pouches, which they carry, but can only access for approved education plans and emergencies. “If there’s an actual emergency, which will be determined by the administration and by the teachers, then they’ll unlock them for use in those emergencies,” Sasaki said. The policy will bring the district into compliance with a state mandate aimed at increasing face-to-face interactions, preventing cyberbullying and limiting distractions in the classroom. Dr. Michael Stanton, a licensed clinical psychologist at CSU East Bay’s Department of Public Health, says 33% of California middle school teachers say that cell phones cause problems in their classrooms. And he adds the issues increase as the kids get older, with 72% of high school teachers reporting distractions and other problems with phones. “Bullying online, people being incredibly distracted during school time, so I think there are some really big pluses from this,” he said. He notes, however, that some of the greatest benefits may be for the younger students. “Focusing on the ‘in person’ can be incredibly helpful for students, especially in the developing ages, where students are learning social relationships, learning how to interact with others,” Stanton said. Mario Oliveros agrees there are benefits, but he says “the jury is still out” for him because he says smartphones are also helpful in the classroom. “For kids, for example, with disabilities, it would be really good for them to have access to their devices. A lot of apps and assisted reading features would be good for them. I think there’s also a case to be made for some useful ed-tech apps, for kids to learn,” he said. Under the new policy, phones will be allowed for documented medical needs, individual education plans and will be unlocked for serious safety or emergency situations.

headlines.title: San Francisco man loses thousands of dollars in alleged rental scam
headlines.description: An engineer in San Francisco said he lost more than $18,000 after someone pretended to be a listing agent and sent him to a real open house. Alvin Tran found a two-bedroom listing in the city on both Zillow and Craigslist. He was interested, so he sent some messages. He got a response from the post on Craigslist; turns out that Craigslist post was fake, copied from the real Zillow listing. However, Tran didn’t know that yet, and started texting with the alleged scammer. Tran says he went to the open house and talked to someone with the same name as the person he’d been messaging. After that, Tran submitted an application, which was accepted. He then wired more than $18,000 and after that, things started to unravel. Erin West, a former Santa Clara County deputy DA and the head of a nonprofit called Operation Shamrock, working to disrupt scam networks joined NBC Bay Area’s Raj Mathai to learn more about these new scams and what to do when encountering one. Watch the full interview in the video above.

headlines.title: High school campus in Richmond shuts down over discovery of toxic chemicals
headlines.description: The West Contra Costa Unified School District shut down the Kennedy High School campus this week over the discovery of toxic chemicals underneath the campus, just less than two weeks before classes begin. Kennedy High School was already one of four high schools undergoing upgrades ahead of the new school year. Now, with students scheduled to return Aug. 18, it’s unclear whether they’ll be back on campus after the district shut down the Richmond school over the discovery of varying levels of tetrachloroethylene, or PCE, beneath the campus, raising concerns for teachers and families. “This really creates an increase stabilizing effect on the entire Kennedy community,” United Teachers of Richmond President Francisco Ortiz said. According to the EPA, PCE is a chemical commonly used in dry cleaning and metal degreasing. Teachers say they’re still waiting for answers about potential health risks and whether other campuses will also be tested. They say they learned Tuesday the school was closing, even though the district says it received the test results Friday and decided to close the campus Monday. “Wanting to have a stable start to the school year and the faster we can get teachers information and the faster we can act accordingly, provide students and family with a solid start to the school year, that would be my hope and my request for the district,” Ortiz said. In a statement to the community, Superintendent Cheryl Cotton said, “The district is exploring options for temporarily relocating the Kennedy High School community in support of a safe and healthy start to the school year.” Read the entire statement below. “The concern is the health of the community. We need to learn the amount of gas that is escaping and what DTSC plans to do about it,” Richmond Mayor Edwardo Martinez said. For parents, uncertainty is adding to the stress. Anna Guerrero recently moved to Richmond and went to the district office on Wednesday to enroll her daughter at Kennedy. She says she was told to complete the paperwork and wait, while the district decides what happens next. “They couldn’t tell me if my daughter can attend another school besides Kennedy. Now we’re just waiting,” she said. The Department of Toxic Substances Control says the PCE was found in soil gas and that they are working on additional testing to determine any safety concerns and the source of the chemical. In a statement, they said in part, “DTSC is working with the school district to test air inside the buildings to ensure that it is not affected by PCE.” Read the entire statement below. Mayor Martinez says the city and district are working together on the issue. “Trust the city, DTSC and school district to alert them of any dangers should there be any to the community nearby. We are doing our very best to make sure that the situation is taken care of,” he said. The school district is hosting a town hall Thursday from 6:30 p.m. to 8 p.m. at the Richmond auditorium to provide an update. Superintendent Cheryl Cotton statement: Dear WCCUSD Community, In response to a recommendation by the Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC), our Board approved third-party testing for underground vapors at the Kennedy High School campus at the July 15 regular board meeting. On Friday, July 31, the WCCUSD Executive Team received preliminary results from this testing, which showed varying levels of tetrachloroethylene (PCE) underground below the Kennedy High School campus. We immediately notified our Board on Friday and began reaching out to the DTSC for assistance understanding these preliminary results. We also began reaching out to local, county, and state officials to make aligned decisions in partnership. Additional testing is needed to determine the risk level within the Kennedy school buildings and on our grounds. Following consultation with DTSC and other agencies on the morning of Monday, August 3, and out of an abundance of caution, WCCUSD made the determination to restrict entry to the Kennedy campus until further environmental testing has been completed and analyzed. As the school year begins on August 18, the District is exploring options for temporarily relocating the Kennedy High School community in support of a safe and healthy start to the school year. Kennedy staff and students should continue to expect regular updates via ParentSquare, and members of the public should follow official WCCUSD social media channels to stay updated. We will be holding a cross-agency town hall with the DTSC and the City of Richmond regarding the ongoing environmental testing on Thursday, August 6, from 6:30pm to 8pm at the Richmond Auditorium at 403 Civic Center Plaza in Richmond. Doors will open at 6:00pm. This event will also be livestreamed via our WCCUSD YouTube channel. We want to thank all agencies at the local, county, and state level who have offered assistance and support of our Kennedy community, as well as members of our local business and philanthropic community. In partnership, Superintendent Cheryl Cotton. Department of Toxic Substances Control statement: DTSC is working closely with the West Contra Costa Unified School District and the City of Richmond in response to recent sampling detecting tetrachloroethylene (PCE) in soil gas at Kennedy High School, which is currently unoccupied. Public safety is our top priority, and additional testing is being done to evaluate any safety concerns in the buildings at Kennedy High School. We are investigating the source of the PCE in the soil and will provide additional information as it becomes available. To protect those who study and work at the school, DTSC is working with the school district to test the air inside the buildings to ensure that it is not affected by PCE and it is safe for students and staff to return to school on August 18.

headlines.title: Several San Ramon businesses burglarized
headlines.description: San Ramon police were investigating a series of business burglaries that happened early Tuesday morning. Police said officers initially responded at about 4:10 a.m. to Utopia Tanning Salon regarding a glass break alarm. While on the scene, several other burglaries were discovered, police said. Other affected businesses included The Saffron Grill, Club Pilates, Pizza My Heart and Supercuts. Surveillance footage of the break-ins was being examined by police in hopes of finding leads on possible suspects, police said. Anyone with information is asked to call police at 925-973-2779.

headlines.title: Alameda County settles with family of 8-year-old killed in child abuse case
headlines.description: Alameda County reached a settlement with the family of an 8-year-old girl who died after child welfare allegedly failed to intervene in her neglect and abuse by her mother. “Sophia Mason was an 8-year-old girl who deserved protection and a full life,” the Alameda County Board of Supervisors said in a statement on behalf of the entire board Tuesday. “We mourn with her grandmother and extended family for what could have been.” Sophia died in her Merced home in 2022, a year after being taken into the custody of her mother. Throughout this time, Alameda County received seven emergency hotline referrals saying Sophia was suffering abuse at home, according to a legal claim filed by attorneys representing her grandmother. In 2023, Sophia’s mother pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter, child abuse and causing great bodily injury in connection with her death. As part of the settlement, the county will pay $12 million to Sylvia Johnson, Sophia’s grandmother, and dedicate a park bench to Sophia. The county also commissioned an independent investigation into its failures handling Sophia’s case that led to 25 suggestions for reform. Among the deficiencies found in the resulting report was that social workers did not respond to and investigate all allegations of suspected child abuse or neglect. Child welfare workers also failed to cross-report to law enforcement, despite being mandated reporters. Miranda Counseling & Consulting, which was contracted for the investigation, proposed greater oversight, injury documentation and internal auditing. Alameda County’s Social Services Agency will “undergo extensive new training, be held to new documentation standards, and new accountability for oversight and accuracy in safety and risk assessments,” supervisors wrote in the statement.

headlines.title: San Bruno Post Office robbery: Public told to check financial accounts, $150K reward issued
headlines.description: The U.S. Postal Inspection Service is offering a reward of up to $150,000 for information leading to the arrest and conviction of the person or people who stole mail from the San Bruno Post Office last week. The robbery at the post office, located at 1300 Huntington Ave., happened between 4:55 p.m. and 5:10 p.m. last Thursday, officials said. At least one person entered the post office, took four tubs of mail and assaulted a postal employee, according to officials. Officials said more mail was taken Wednesday morning. It wasn’t immediately known if the thefts were related. “This time it was three individuals came back in a different vehicle but same modus operandi as we call it,” U.S. Postal Inspector Matthew Norfleet said. Officials said mail thieves are almost entirely looking for financial instruments they can exploit. “Checks, credit cards, things like that,” Norfleet said. “Anybody who is in the San Bruno area, if they mailed a check that didn’t get where it was going or if they were expecting a check that they didn’t get in their mail, those would be valuable leads for our investigators.” Police said residents should monitor their financial accounts for any unauthorized activity. Those who believe their mail may have been stolen or compromised are instructed to file a report with the U.S. Postal Inspection Service (reference case No. 4750763-ROBB).

headlines.title: Outside Lands 2026: Performers, food vendors, activities and what to know
headlines.description: The annual three-day San Francisco music festival, Outside Lands, kicks off Friday. Here’s what to know ahead of the highly-anticipated event. Where will Outside Lands be held? The festival will be held at Golden Gate Park and will host over 90 artists and 100 food and drink vendors. San Francisco Aug 4 San Francisco May 6 Who is performing at Outside Lands? Headliners include Charli XCX, The Strokes, PinkPanthress, Rüfüs Du Sol and Empire of the Sun. Other performers include Labyrinth, GloRilla, Djo and Geese. The earliest acts begin at 12 p.m. each day and the latest performances will start at 10 p.m. Visit the schedule page to view all performers and their set times. What will the food menu offer at Outside Lands? Various food and drink locations will also be available at the festival. Locations are spread across the festival with options for multiple dietary restrictions. Special drink locations at the festival include Cocktail Magic, Wine Lands and Beer Lands. Visit the full list of food and drink options on Outside Land’s website. Outside Lands transportation: What to know Transportation is another factor that the festival urges fans to consider. There is no general admission parking at the festival. Outside Lands recommends that festivalgoers leave their cars at home and utilize public transportation. The festival offers shuttle passes, picking up fans from Bill Graham Civic Auditorium in San Francisco. Other modes of transportation to consider include Muni, BART, and rideshare services. Outside Lands bag policy Festivalgoers are also warned about Outside Lands bag policy. The following bag types are allowed, per Outside Lands webpage: Backpacks and bags made of clear plastic, clear vinyl, or clear PVC Small bags, fanny-packs, purses up to 6” x 8” x 3” (do not have to be clear) Empty dedicated hydration packs with a bladder capacity of under 2.5 liters or 150 inches, and no more than one additional pocket. Standard size backpacks with hydration bladders will not be permitted. Other FAQ answers are available to view in the information section. Are tickets still available for Outside Lands? Limited tickets remain and are at a high resale price. To secure legitimate tickets, Outside Lands provides access to their Official Resale Marketplace. If you are unable to visit the festival in person, it will be streamed on Amazon Music, Prime Video, Twitch, Fire TV and Samsung TV Plus. headlines.title: Major closures coming to Carquinez Bridge
headlines.description: Major closures are coming to the Carquinez Bridge, which connects Vallejo to the East Bay. The bridge is set for a full deck replacement. Caltrans said crews need to repave the bridge to ensure safety and smoothness. Crews will begin repairs at 6 p.m. Friday, resulting in one westbound lane closure. The repair is expected to continue until 7 p.m. Saturday. A full bridge closure will start two weeks later on Aug. 21. Lanes will reopen on Aug. 24.
